assessments.reasoning: The exact CIRCABC URL rendered seven pages. Page 1 identifies v.1.0 twice, and Article 13 on page 5 contains its distinctive awareness-of-publication wording. Integrity was assessed for the rendering.

Recitals 1–3 distinguish v.1.0 from its v.1.1 revision. This is Commission evidence of edition history. The annex supplies v.1.2. [Decision (EU) 2017/863, p. 1](https://interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/custom-page/attachment/eupl_v1.2_en.pdf)

The pinned Index decision matches UUID ffed73335f9049c989a885a2f0c6f829, display name, kind, edition scope, documentary revision and URL. Its opening paragraph states the admission and review condition.

The pinned scope admits historical licence editions with identifiable text and controlling evidence. It establishes the Index’s authority over classification. The edition-specific assignment comes from the editorial decision.

challenge.method: Tested whether the filename could conceal a different edition, whether the 2017 decision supplied a replacement text, and whether the editorial row recorded an already active entity. Compared the opening notice, Articles 5 and 13, and the prospective entity ID.
challenge.results: The notice and both articles distinguish this rendering from v.1.1. The 2017 decision identifies v.1.0 in its recitals and releases v.1.2 in its sole article. The editorial row matches the subject and expressly conditions activation on qualification. No material contradiction was found.

limitations: The Commission observation covers the rendered English edition. The browser returned no original PDF bytes or PDF digest.

The qualification condition appears in the statement and the cited decision. Reading `state` in isolation from them would overstate the finding. Completion of the admission and review gates was outside this review.
The filename and copyright year do not settle adoption chronology. Language equivalence, redistribution, installation and grants for particular works are outside scope.
reasoning: The CIRCABC document identifies itself as EUPL v.1.0 in both its title and its opening notice. The Index decision assigns the matching prospective entity the display name European Union Public Licence v. 1.0, kind `license`, and state `active` upon qualification.
